nodes.label: python-chess Pin-Agnostic Attack Maps
nodes.author: Michael Farrugia
nodes.rationale: python-chess directly supports FEN, UCI moves, board validation, and geometric attacker semantics that count pinned pieces, avoiding the correctness risk of custom rules and duplicated browser rules.

nodes.label: Immutable Catalog with Precomputed Answers
nodes.author: Michael Farrugia
nodes.rationale: A versioned build-time catalog makes the 100-position set reproducible, removes runtime Lichess dependency, keeps submission deterministic, and preserves provenance and rule-version reviewability.

nodes.label: SQLite as Progress Authority
nodes.author: Michael Farrugia
nodes.rationale: SQLite transactions and uniqueness constraints prevent phantom or duplicate attempts while keeping data local and avoiding a separate service or custom file-locking scheme.

nodes.label: Custom Accessible Selection Board
nodes.author: Michael Farrugia
nodes.rationale: The product selects pieces but never moves them, so an 8x8 semantic button grid gives direct control over overlapping marker and eligibility states with native keyboard and focus semantics.

nodes.label: Loopback-Only Same-Origin Runtime
nodes.author: Michael Farrugia
nodes.rationale: The application is personal and local, so binding to 127.0.0.1, serving local assets, disabling CORS, and validating mutation origins prevents arbitrary cross-origin writes without introducing authentication scope.

nodes.label: Flask and Server-Rendered Shell
nodes.author: Michael Farrugia
nodes.rationale: One focused screen and small progress views fit Flask, Jinja, vanilla JavaScript, and CSS; a single Python process reduces setup, build lifecycle, and offline integration complexity.
